en pølse.explanation: "En pølse" means "a sausage". To order a hot dog, say: "Jeg vil gerne have en hotdog" (I would like a hot dog). A street stand that sells them is "en pølsevogn" (a hot dog stand).

en pølsevogn.explanation: "En pølsevogn" means "a hot dog stand". It is built from "en pølse" (a sausage) and "en vogn" (a wagon). "Vogn" is also in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart) and "en barnevogn" (a stroller).

et palads.explanation: "Et palads" means "a palace". To talk about a palace in a story, say: "Prinsessen bor i et palads" (The princess lives in a palace). Do not mix it up with "et slot" (a castle). The royal family's home in Copenhagen is "Amalienborg Slot".

et par.explanation: "Et par" means "a couple / a pair". To talk about two things that belong together, say: "et par sko" (a pair of shoes). To say a small number, put it before a noun: "et par dage" (a couple of days). To talk about two people in a relationship, say: "De er et sødt par" (They are a sweet couple).

et par jeans.explanation: "Et par jeans" means "a pair of jeans". To say what colour they are, put the colour after "et par": "et par sorte jeans" (a pair of black jeans). To say you are wearing jeans, leave out "et par": "Jeg har jeans på" (I am wearing jeans).

et paradis.explanation: "Et paradis" means "a paradise". To say a place is a paradise for a certain group, use "for": "et paradis for børn" (a paradise for children).

et paraplystativ.explanation: "Et paraplystativ" means "an umbrella stand". It is built from "en paraply" (an umbrella) and "et stativ" (a stand).

et parkeringshus.explanation: "Et parkeringshus" means "a parking garage". It is built from "en parkering" (parking) and "et hus" (a house).

et parti.explanation: "Et parti" means "a party", as in a political party. To talk about one game of chess, use it for a game: "Vi spiller et parti skak" (We are playing a game of chess). For a party with food and music, use "en fest" (a party): "Vi holder fest i morgen" (We are having a party tomorrow).

et pas.explanation: "Et pas" means "a passport". To ask to see one, say: "Må jeg se dit pas?" (May I see your passport?). Do not mix it up with "at passe" (to fit): "Skoen passer" (The shoe fits).

et pasfoto.explanation: "Et pasfoto" means "a passport photo". It is built from "et pas" (a passport) and "et foto" (a photo). "Foto" is also in "et fotoalbum" (a photo album).

et penalhus.explanation: "Et penalhus" means "a pencil case". It ends in "hus" (house), as in "et parkeringshus" (a parking garage).

et pengeskab.explanation: "Et pengeskab" means "a safe". It is built from "penge" (money) and "et skab" (a cupboard). "Skab" is also in "et køleskab" (a refrigerator).

et pensum.explanation: "Et pensum" means "a syllabus". To say something is not part of the course material, use "ikke på pensum" (not on the syllabus): "Det kapitel er ikke på pensum" (That chapter is not on the syllabus).

et personalemøde.explanation: "Et personalemøde" means "a staff meeting". It is built from "personale" (staff) and "et møde" (a meeting). "Møde" is also in "et forældremøde" (a parents' meeting).

et perspektiv.explanation: "Et perspektiv" means "a perspective". To say someone's view is interesting, say: "Det er et interessant perspektiv" (That is an interesting perspective). In drawing, it means making a flat picture look deep: "Tegn huset i perspektiv" (Draw the house in perspective).

et pindsvin.explanation: "Et pindsvin" means "a hedgehog". Literally, it is a "stick hog".

et piskeris.explanation: "Et piskeris" means "a whisk". It is built from "at piske" (to whip) and "ris" (twigs).

et plaster.explanation: "Et plaster" means "a band-aid". To talk about a pack of band-aids, use the plural form "plastre": "en pakke plastre" (a pack of band-aids).

et plejebarn.explanation: "Et plejebarn" means "a foster child". It is built from "pleje" (care) and "et barn" (a child). Do not mix it up with "et adoptivbarn" (an adopted child): "De har et adoptivbarn fra Kina" (They have an adopted child from China).

et point.explanation: "Et point" means "a point", as in a game or test. To say how many you scored, say: "Hun fik ti point" (She got ten points). To make a point in an argument, use "en pointe": "Det var en god pointe" (That was a good point).

et postbud.explanation: "Et postbud" means "a mail carrier". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et bud" (a messenger).

et posthus.explanation: "Et posthus" means "a post office". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et hus" (a house). To say you are going there, say: "Jeg skal på posthuset" (I am going to the post office).

et postkontor.explanation: "Et postkontor" means "a post office". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et kontor" (an office). To say you are going there, say: "Jeg skal på postkontoret" (I am going to the post office).

et postkort.explanation: "Et postkort" means "a postcard". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et kort" (a card). "Kort" is also in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

et postnummer.explanation: "Et postnummer" means "a postal code". It is built from "post" (mail) and "et nummer" (a number). To write a Danish address, put the four-digit postal code before the town: "2100 København Ø" (2100 Copenhagen Ø).

et potentiale.explanation: "Et potentiale" means "a potential". To say something has potential in general, leave out "et": "Der er potentiale i idéen" (There is potential in the idea).

et princip.explanation: "Et princip" means "a principle". To say you do something because of your beliefs, use "af princip" (on principle): "Jeg spiser ikke kød af princip" (I do not eat meat on principle). To say something is true in theory, use "i princip" (in principle): "I princip kan alle komme" (In principle, anyone can come).

et prisfald.explanation: "Et prisfald" means "a price drop". It is built from "en pris" (a price) and "et fald" (a fall). "Fald" is also in "et snefald" (a snowfall).

et prisskilt.explanation: "Et prisskilt" means "a price tag". It is built from "en pris" (a price) and "et skilt" (a sign). "Skilt" is also in "et gadeskilt" (a street sign).

et problem.explanation: "Et problem" means "a problem". To say "no problem" when someone thanks you or asks a favor, say: "Det er ikke noget problem" (It is no problem).

et produkt.explanation: "Et produkt" means "a product". To say where a product comes from, put the country adjective before it: "et dansk produkt" (a Danish product).

et program.explanation: "Et program" means "a program", as on a computer. When you ask what is planned for the day, it means "schedule": "Hvad er programmet i dag?" (What is the plan today?)

et projekt.explanation: "Et projekt" means "a project". To say you are beginning one, say: "Vi starter et nyt projekt i dag" (We are starting a new project today).

et prøverum.explanation: "Et prøverum" means "a fitting room". It is built from "at prøve" (to try) and "et rum" (a room).

et pseudonym.explanation: "Et pseudonym" means "a pseudonym". To ask for an author's pen name, say: "Hvad er hendes pseudonym?" (What is her pseudonym?) Do not mix it up with "anonym" (anonymous), which means no name is given at all: "Brevet er anonymt" (The letter is anonymous).

et pudebetræk.explanation: "Et pudebetræk" means "a pillowcase". It is built from "en pude" (a pillow) and "et betræk" (a cover). "Betræk" is also in "et sofabetræk" (a sofa cover).

et pulver.explanation: "Et pulver" means "a powder". It is also the last part of "bagepulver" (baking powder).

et pund.explanation: "Et pund" means "a pound", as in British money. When you buy food by weight, "et pund" is 500 grams: "Jeg køber et pund smør" (I am buying 500 grams of butter).

et punkt.explanation: "Et punkt" means "a point / spot". To name a weak spot, say: "et svagt punkt" (a weak point). Do not mix it up with "et punktum" (a period): "Sæt et punktum efter sætningen" (Put a period after the sentence).

et punktum.explanation: "Et punktum" means "a period", as in the punctuation mark. To say a matter is closed, say "Punktum!" (That's final!): "Jeg har sagt nej, punktum!" (I said no, period!)

et puslespil.explanation: "Et puslespil" means "a puzzle". To say you are doing one, use "at lægge" (to put): "Vi lægger et puslespil" (We are doing a puzzle). Do not mix it up with "en gåde" (a riddle): "Kan du løse den gåde?" (Can you solve that riddle?)

et påfund.explanation: "Et påfund" means "an idea / invention". It comes from "at finde på" (to think up). To ask what someone has come up with, say: "Hvad er det for et påfund?" (What kind of idea is that?)

et påskeæg.explanation: "Et påskeæg" means "an Easter egg". It is built from "påske" (Easter) and "et æg" (an egg). In Denmark, someone who guesses who sent a "gækkebrev" (a teasing Easter letter) wins an Easter egg.

pandehår.explanation: "Et pandehår" means "bangs". It is built from "en pande" (a forehead) and "et hår" (a hair). To say someone has bangs, leave out "et": "Hun har pandehår" (She has bangs).

panik.explanation: "Panik" means "panic". To say someone suddenly panicked, use "at gå i panik" (to panic): "Hun gik i panik" (She panicked).

pant.explanation: "Pant" means "deposit". In Denmark, you get the "pant" back when you return an empty bottle or can to a shop.

pap.explanation: "Pap" means "cardboard". To say what something is cut from, say: "Han klipper en figur ud af pap" (He cuts a shape out of cardboard). Do not mix it up with "papir" (paper): "Jeg skriver på papir" (I write on paper).

papir.explanation: "Papir" means "a paper". To talk about the material, leave out "et": "Vi bruger ikke plastik, kun papir" (We do not use plastic, only paper). In the plural, "papirer" also means "documents": "Har du dine papirer med?" (Do you have your papers with you?)

paradoksal.explanation: "Paradoksal" means "paradoxical". It comes from the noun "et paradoks" (a paradox).

paranoid.explanation: "Paranoid" means "paranoid". To tell someone they are being too suspicious, say: "Du er helt paranoid" (You are totally paranoid).

parat.explanation: "Parat" means "ready". To say people are standing by, use it with "stå" (to stand): "Politiet står parat" (The police stand ready).

parkeret.explanation: "Parkeret" means "parked". It comes from the verb "at parkere" (to park). To say a car is parked where it is not allowed, add "ulovligt" (illegally): "ulovligt parkeret" (illegally parked).

parkering.explanation: "Parkering" means "parking". It comes from the verb "at parkere" (to park). To say you are looking for a space, use "finde" (to find): "Det er svært at finde parkering" (It is hard to find parking).

parmesan.explanation: "Parmesan" means "parmesan". Danish also has "parmesanost" (parmesan cheese), built from "parmesan" and "en ost" (a cheese).

pas på.explanation: "Pas på" means "watch out". To warn someone about danger, say: "Pas på, det er varmt" (Watch out, it is hot). To tell someone to look after other people, say: "Pas på børnene" (Look after the children).

pas på dig selv.explanation: "Pas på dig selv" means "take care". To end a talk with a wish for the other person, say: "Tak for i dag. Pas på dig selv!" (Thanks for today. Take care!) To say it to several people, use "pas på jer selv" (take care of yourselves).

passende.explanation: "Passende" means "suitable". To say something is the right thing to do, say: "Det er ikke passende at komme for sent" (It is not appropriate to come late). To tell someone to dress for an occasion, say: "Tag passende tøj på" (Put on suitable clothes).

passiv.explanation: "Passiv" means "passive". In grammar, "passiv" names a sentence form where the action happens to the subject: "Bilen blev stjålet" (The car was stolen).

pasta.explanation: "Pasta" means "pasta". Its "the" form "pastaen" shows that it takes "en". When you talk about pasta in general, leave "en" out: "Jeg laver pasta" (I am making pasta).

peber.explanation: "Peber" means "pepper", as in the spice. To say you season food with it, say: "Jeg bruger peber på kødet" (I use pepper on the meat). Do not mix it up with "peberfrugt" (bell pepper), a vegetable: "Jeg skærer en peberfrugt i tern" (I cut a bell pepper into cubes).

penge.explanation: "Penge" means "money". To say you have none, say: "Jeg har ingen penge" (I have no money). To talk about one coin, use "en mønt" (a coin): "Jeg har en mønt i lommen" (I have a coin in my pocket).

pensioneret.explanation: "Pensioneret" means "retired". It comes from "en pension" (a pension).

perfekt.explanation: "Perfekt" means "perfect". To agree to a plan with one word, reply: "Perfekt. Så ses vi klokken otte." (Perfect. See you at eight.)

permanent.explanation: "Permanent" means "permanent". The opposite is "midlertidig" (temporary): "en midlertidig løsning" (a temporary solution).

persille.explanation: "Persille" means "parsley". To say it is chopped, add "hakket" (chopped): "hakket persille" (chopped parsley).

personale.explanation: "Et personale" means "staff". To talk about one person who works there, use "en medarbejder" (an employee): "Vi har en ny medarbejder" (We have a new employee).

personlig.explanation: "Personlig" means "personal". To say a question touches someone's private life, say: "Det er et personligt spørgsmål" (That is a personal question). To say something has its own character, say: "en personlig stil" (a personal style).

personligt.explanation: "Personligt" means "personally". To give your own opinion, put it at the start of the sentence: "Personligt synes jeg, at det er for dyrt" (Personally, I think it is too expensive). To say in person, put it after the verb: "Jeg har mødt hende personligt" (I have met her in person).

pervers.explanation: "Pervers" means "perverted". It is a strong word, so be careful when you use it about a person. To say something is absurdly against what is reasonable, say: "Det er pervers, at vi smider mad ud" (It is perverse that we throw food away).

pessimistisk.explanation: "Pessimistisk" means "pessimistic". To say a person expects the worst, say: "Hun er pessimistisk" (She is pessimistic). To say a forecast looks bad, say: "en pessimistisk prognose" (a pessimistic forecast).

pinlig.explanation: "Pinlig" means "embarrassing". It describes the situation, not your feeling. To say how you feel, use "flov" (embarrassed): "Jeg er flov" (I am embarrassed).

pinse.explanation: "En pinse" means "Pentecost". In Denmark, the Monday after is called "anden pinsedag" (the second day of Pentecost).

piskefløde.explanation: "Piskefløde" means "whipping cream". It is built from "at piske" (to whip) and "fløde" (cream). For cream in your coffee, ask for "kaffefløde" (coffee cream): "Må jeg få lidt kaffefløde?" (May I have a little coffee cream?)

pjat.explanation: "Pjat" means "nonsense". To say someone is talking nonsense, use "at tale pjat" (to talk nonsense): "Han taler pjat" (He is talking nonsense).

placeret.explanation: "Placeret" means "located". To say where a building is, say: "Biblioteket er placeret ved havnen" (The library is located by the harbor). To say someone has a high rank, add "højt" (high): "en højt placeret politiker" (a high-ranking politician).

pladsmangel.explanation: "En pladsmangel" means "a lack of space". It is built from "en plads" (a space) and "en mangel" (a lack). "Mangel" is also in "vandmangel" (water shortage).

planlægning.explanation: "Planlægning" means "planning". Do not mix it up with "en plan" (a plan), which is the result: "Vi har en plan" (We have a plan). The work before it is "planlægning": "Rejsen kræver god planlægning" (The trip needs good planning).

plastik.explanation: "Plastik" means "plastic". It is also the first part of "plastikaffald" (plastic waste) and "en plastikflaske" (a plastic bottle).

plastikaffald.explanation: "Plastikaffald" means "plastic waste". It is built from "plastik" (plastic) and "et affald" (waste). "Affald" is also in "madaffald" (food waste).

plat.explanation: "Plat" means "cheesy". When you flip a coin, "plat" is also the word for one side: "Krone eller plat?" (Heads or tails?)

pleje.explanation: "En pleje" means "care", as in looking after someone who is ill. The verb "at pleje" means "to nurse": "Hun plejer sin syge mor" (She nurses her sick mother). It also means "to be in the habit of": "Jeg plejer at stå tidligt op" (I usually get up early).

pludselig.explanation: "Pludselig" means "suddenly". Before a noun, it means "sudden": "en pludselig lyd" (a sudden sound).

poesi.explanation: "En poesi" means "poetry". It can also mean a beautiful, dreamlike quality in a place: "Der er poesi i den gamle by" (There is poetry in the old town).

polen.explanation: "Polen" means "Poland". To say you are going there, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Polen" (We are traveling to Poland). To say you are there, use "i" (in): "Hun bor i Polen" (She lives in Poland).

politi.explanation: "Politi" means "police". To say "the police", add "-et": "Politiet er her" (The police are here). To talk about one officer, use "en politibetjent" (a police officer): "En politibetjent hjælper os" (A police officer is helping us).

politisk.explanation: "Politisk" means "political". To describe a debate, say: "en politisk debat" (a political debate). The subject itself is "politik" (politics): "Han interesserer sig for politik" (He is interested in politics).

polsk.explanation: "Polsk" means "Polish". In English "Polish" starts with "P", but Danish "polsk" starts with "p", even for the language: "Jeg taler polsk" (I speak Polish).

polyester.explanation: "En polyester" means "polyester". It can start a longer word for clothes: "en polyestertrøje" (a polyester sweater).

pommes frites.explanation: "Pommes frites" means "French fries". To order them in a short way, say "pommes" (fries): "En burger og pommes, tak" (A burger and fries, please).

popcorn.explanation: "Popcorn" means "popcorn". To suggest making it, use "lave" (to make): "Skal vi lave popcorn?" (Shall we make popcorn?)

populær.explanation: "Populær" means "popular". To say who likes it, use "blandt" (among): "Sangen er populær blandt børn" (The song is popular with children).

porcelæn.explanation: "Et porcelæn" means "porcelain". To talk about the best dishes, say "det fine porcelæn" (the good china): "Vi bruger det fine porcelæn til jul" (We use the good china at Christmas).

porto.explanation: "Porto" means "postage". To ask about the cost of sending something, say: "Hvad koster porto til Sverige?" (What does postage to Sweden cost?)

positiv.explanation: "Positiv" means "positive". To talk about good news, say: "positive nyheder" (positive news). To say a person is upbeat, say: "Hun er meget positiv" (She is very upbeat). The opposite is "negativ" (negative): "et negativt svar" (a negative answer).

positivt.explanation: "Positivt" means "positively". To say how someone spoke about something, say: "Hun talte positivt om projektet" (She spoke positively about the project). To tell someone to stay hopeful, say: "Tænk positivt!" (Think positively!)

post.explanation: "Post" means "mail". To talk about mail in general, leave out "en": "Jeg har fået post" (I have received mail). It is also the first part of "et postkort" (a postcard).

pragtfuld.explanation: "Pragtfuld" means "splendid". It is built from "pragt" (splendor) and "-fuld" (full of). To praise a view, say: "en pragtfuld solnedgang" (a splendid sunset).

praktisk.explanation: "Praktisk" means "practical". To say it is handy to do something, say: "Det er praktisk at bo tæt på stationen" (It is practical to live close to the station). To say a person is good with their hands, say: "Jeg er ikke så praktisk" (I am not very handy).

pressefrihed.explanation: "Pressefrihed" means "freedom of the press". It is built from "presse" (press) and "frihed" (freedom).
